title: AtlasPay POC scoping - workload & benchmarks
summary: POC scoping to align on success criteria and traffic model for AtlasPay's fraud-detection and routing assistant. Agreed target QPS/concurrency for initial benchmark, token distributions, and a 2-week pilot timeline with security doc exchange.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark template and load test harness link
AtlasPay to provide sample traffic CSV and typical prompt set
Redwood SE to propose instance types and expected throughput by model
action_items: Jordan Park: send pricing sheet and PCI/KMS notes - due 2026-10-09
Maya Chen: prepare benchmark config and expected metrics (QPS/concurrency/latency targets) - due 2026-10-12
Sofia Alvarez: upload sample prompts and token distribution CSV - due 2026-10-09

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (AtlasPay Head of ML), Sofia Alvarez (AtlasPay Infra), Tom Baker (AtlasPay PM)

Summary (auto): Scoping POC for workload characterization and benchmarking. Focus areas: QPS targets, concurrency, input/output token distribution, latency SLOs, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, security gating.

[00:00] Jordan Park: hey everyone thanks for joining i think we got everyone on the call, quick intros, i'll let maya do a quick agenda?
[00:12] Maya Chen: yeah hi all maya redwood se, i'll run through how we model qps + concurrency and then propose benchmark plan, also will cover caching/batching considerations and what metrics we collect.
[00:25] Rajiv Menon: rajiv - we own the fraud model and routing assistant, mainly using generative scoring to surface reasons for flags. key for us is 95th percentile latency under load and cost per 1M tokens.
[00:40] Sofia Alvarez: sofia infra, we care about VPC peering, network egress, and customer-managed KMS.
[00:45] Tom Baker: tom product, timeline is tight — want pilot in prod-ish env in 2 weeks, success = 99% accuracy retention and latency under 300ms p95 if possible.

[01:10] Maya Chen: ok quick qual — what does current traffic look like? qps, payload size, concurrency?
[01:20] Rajiv Menon: currently our synchronous scoring service sits at avg 80 qps during peak, spiky up to 160 qps for short bursts. concurrency around 40 active requests. prompts are mid-length: avg input tokens ~120, outputs ~80, but some edge cases go to 800 tokens when we run enriched context.
[01:45] Jordan Park: perfect that gives us a baseline. for a poc we usually recommend modeling a couple of tiers: baseline (avg qps), peak sustained (1.5-2x), and spike test (2-3x for short windows). so maybe baseline 80 qps, sustained 140 qps, spike 240 qps for 60s.
[02:10] Rajiv Menon: that sounds realistic. what's the concurrency mapping to qps for latency sensitive calls?
[02:20] Maya Chen: depends on model and batching. on hosted low-latency models with no batching you can treat qps ~ concurrency * (1 / latency). with batching you get pennies per token but higher latency variability; for fraud decisions we recommend minimal batching and kv caching where possible.
[02:50] Sofia Alvarez: can you explain kv cash? i heard that in your doc, is that the same as kv cache?
[02:55] Maya Chen: yeah that's a transcription hiccup — kv cache; it's the key/value cache for autoregressive models to avoid recomputing earlier tokens. saves a lot on long contexts.

[03:30] Jordan Park: success criteria — what are the 3 things we need to sign off pilot?
[03:36] Tom Baker: 1) Latency p95 < 300ms for 80 qps baseline, 2) Model quality (we'll provide eval dataset) no more than 2% drop vs current, 3) Cost per decision within our target (we'll share target later).
[03:55] Rajiv Menon: add reliability: fallbacks in case of overload and audit logs for every inference.

[04:15] Maya Chen: noted. on tokens distribution — can you confirm typical prompt composition? e.g. structured fields + recent events + user note?
[04:26] Rajiv Menon: yep structured header ~30 tokens, recent events ~200 tokens sometimes, user note ~50 tokens. we anonymize PII before sending. avg input 120 is after trimming. outputs typically short explanations ~40-120 tokens.

[05:00] Maya Chen: ideal for modeling: give us a CSV sample with columns: timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, is_enriched_context(true/false). that lets us synthesize traffic and produce expected token volume and storage egress estimates.
[05:20] Sofia Alvarez: we can do that, i'll scrub and upload by friday.

[06:00] Maya Chen: metrics to collect in bench: qps, concurrency, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, gpu utilization, system CPU, network egress, and failed rates. also measure cold-start behavior for private nodes.

[06:35] Jordan Park: question about deployment mode — dedicated vs hosted. pros/cons?
[06:43] Maya Chen: hosted gets you fastest onboarding and lower ops but shared tenants; dedicated gives predictable throughput, guaranteed GPU pools, and VPC options. for PCI-like workloads we'd recommend dedicated or private with customer-managed KMS.
[07:05] Rajiv Menon: we have strict network policies, can hosted satisfy that?
[07:12] Jordan Park: hosted can do strict data controls but if you need VPC-only or air-gapped then Private deployment is the route; Dedicated sits in between with private networking options. we'll bring security docs.

[08:00] Tom Baker: benchmark timeline? you suggested a 1-hour load test — what does that look like?
[08:08] Maya Chen: typical run: 15m ramp, 30m steady at target QPS, 15m spike and cool down. we'll run baseline at 80 qps, sustained at 140 qps for 30m, then one or two 60s spikes to 240 qps. collect per-request latencies.
[08:35] Rajiv Menon: for the model variants, we have two candidate checkpoints — base-1 and quant-1. quant-1 is 4-bit quantized, much cheaper but we need quality check. can you run both?
[08:50] Maya Chen: yes we can side-by-side; we'll produce quality delta and throughput. quantization often reduces memory pressure and increases throughput but watch out for small regressions on edge cases.

[09:20] Jordan Park: cost modeling — we provide estimated tokens per second and mapping to expected GPU hours for Dedicated. Maya will produce a spreadsheet mapping token volume to cost per 1M tokens under different batch sizes and quant profiles.

[09:45] Sofia Alvarez: on encryption — do you support customer-managed keys?
[09:50] Maya Chen: yes kms/hsm support for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports encryption-at-rest with redwood keys but we can integrate with customer KMS for Dedicated. we'll attach the network diagram and KMS integration doc.

[10:20] Tom Baker: any concerns with our anonymization step? we do it at app layer before sending.
[10:26] Jordan Park: that's good practice — helps with data residency and PII. we'll also capture retention policies in the security brief.

[11:05] Maya Chen: sample bench config i'll propose: model=base-1 and quant-1, concurrency targets mapped to qps: baseline 80 qps target p95 < 300ms, sustained 140 qps p95 < 500ms, spike 240 qps short p95 < 800ms. batch size should be 1 for latency-sensitive path; optional batching for async scoring paths.

[11:40] Rajiv Menon: can you estimate required GPUs for sustained 140 qps?
[11:46] Maya Chen: rough ballpark depends on model size. for base-1 on A100-class equivalent we might get ~100-150 tokens/s per GPU depending on batch; with input+output average 200 tokens per request (120 in, 80 out) that's ~16k tokens/s for 80 qps, so sustained 140 qps ~28k tokens/s. we'll produce a sizing table but initial guess is 2-3 GPUs for sustained on dedicated optimized instances; quant-1 could drop that to 1-2 GPUs.

[12:30] Jordan Park: ok let's capture expected metrics output from load test: latency distribution, tokens/sec, token cost, GPU utilization, mem pressure, retry/fail rates, and quality delta vs our eval.

[13:00] Tom Baker: for the success criteria if quant-1 shows <1% degradation and halves cost it's acceptable. otherwise base-1 must meet latency/cost targets.

[13:25] Maya Chen: we'll include regression thresholds and a canary rollout plan: start 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions.

[14:00] Sofia Alvarez: audit logs and traceability — need per-request audit for compliance, retained for 90 days at least. is that configurable?

[14:08] Jordan Park: yes retention configurable; we will provide storage cost estimates. Dedicated/Private gives more control over retention location.

[14:40] Rajiv Menon: do you have a test harness we can run in our environment or do we run it from your side?

[14:46] Maya Chen: both options. for network-limited tests we run from AtlasPay infra via a small runner that hits the endpoint; for pure capacity we run from our load rigs. we'll share the harness repo link.

[15:20] Tom Baker: timeline recap?

[15:25] Jordan Park: 1) Atlas uploads sample CSV + eval dataset by 2026-10-09, 2) Redwood shares benchmark template + pricing + security docs by 2026-10-09, 3) SE proposes instance sizing and bench config by 2026-10-12, 4) Schedule 1-hour bench week of 2026-10-12 (target 2026-10-14), 5) Pilot run and results within 48 hours of bench.

[16:00] Maya Chen: any blockers on our side?

[16:05] Sofia Alvarez: need internal approval for sharing tokenized prompts but should be ok, and network peering requires a ticket.

[16:18] Rajiv Menon: give me a template for success criteria to sign off quickly.

[16:28] Jordan Park: we'll send a one-pager for signoff and include explicit metrics and thresholds.

[16:45] Tom Baker: on benchmarks please surface p95 and p99; we need to know tail behavior.

[16:52] Maya Chen: we'll include p50/p95/p99 and 99.9 for long tail; also token latency breakdown and percent of requests served from cache if we can use prefix caching.

[17:20] Rajiv Menon: any mentions of competitors here, i know we evaluated openai and anthro — how are you positioned?

[17:27] Jordan Park: we position as production-first inference platform focusing on predictable economics, dedicated/private deployments, and tooling for rollouts and cost control. we'll share a short battlecard.

[18:00] Maya Chen: quick gotcha — when you provide sample data, include distribution of rare long-context cases so we can model outliers.

[18:25] Sofia Alvarez: noted, we'll add a 'long-tail' column to sample CSV.

[18:40] Jordan Park: ok i think that's most of it, do you want us to also scope a security review call?

[18:47] Sofia Alvarez: yes please, after we review the docs maybe next week.

[19:05] Tom Baker: final ask: can you include an approximate cost delta for quant vs base in the spreadsheet?

[19:12] Maya Chen: yes we will show cost per 1M tokens and per-decision estimates for both.

[19:30] Jordan Park: recap of next steps and action items (see action items list). i'll send calendar invites for the benchmark and security review. thanks everyone.

[19:50] Rajiv Menon: thanks all.

[51:30] End of recording
